overview.overviewText: This chapter explores Linear Momentum of a System of Particles and Centre of Mass Motion, providing comprehensive conceptual analysis, mathematical relationships, and structured applications grounded in NCERT authority.

blocks.title: 1. Key Academic Principles: Linear Momentum of a System of Particles and Centre of Mass Motion
blocks.contentMarkdown: The total linear momentum of a system of particles is equal to the product of total mass M and the velocity of its centre of mass: P_total = M * V_cm. The motion of the centre of mass of a system of particles is governed exclusively by net external force: M * A_cm = F_ext. The sum of all internal forces between constituent particles of an isolated system is zero by Newton's third law.

blocks.title: 2. Key Academic Principles: Linear Momentum of a System of Particles and Centre of Mass Motion
blocks.contentMarkdown: If net external force acting on a system is zero, the velocity of the centre of mass remains constant and total linear momentum is conserved. Internal forces can alter the relative velocities of constituent particles but cannot alter the motion of the centre of mass. The velocity of the centre of mass is given by V_cm = dR_cm/dt = (1/M) * Sum(m_i * v_i).

blocks.title: 3. Key Academic Principles: Linear Momentum of a System of Particles and Centre of Mass Motion
blocks.contentMarkdown: Differentiating with respect to time gives the acceleration of the centre of mass: A_cm = dV_cm/dt = (1/M) * Sum(m_i * a_i). The centre of mass of a system of particles moves as if the entire mass of the system were concentrated at that point and all external forces were applied directly at that point.
